claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the Provider support policy page) that the support index links to.
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes which providers get long-term security updates.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi also ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The page /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists and lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older provider major versions (those not the latest and not covered by the previous-major security updates) receive no patches at all from Pulumi.
The Pulumi Registry (/registry/) lists the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
The page /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists (Provider support policy).
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version (N-1) for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving long-term support updates on eligible older versions are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry pages exist at /registry/packages/aws/, azure/, azure-native/, azuread/, command/, docker-build/, gcp/, kubernetes/, tls/, and vault/.

The LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.
An LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS providers remain compatible with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at unless security fixes prompt otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.
When major N+1 ships, it becomes the new N, the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the old LTS major reaches end of life the same day regardless of remaining 12-month window.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning to a major is recommended.
Older majors than the LTS version receive no patches; if v3 is the newest release, v2 is N-1 and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
End of life versions (N-2 and older) are not supported and receive no updates.
The FAQ page /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ has a section on best practices for maintaining provider versions.
